title: Eval Harness: Prompt Sets Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the standardized process for onboarding new prompt sets into the eval-harness, establishing benchmarks, applying quality guardrails, validating quantization profiles against prompt-driven regressions, and the triage workflow when regressions are detected. It is intended for Applied ML engineers, model owners, and QA engineers who maintain model quality across serving deployments.

Scope

- Applies to all prompt sets that are included in the central prompt catalog and evaluated by the eval-harness (redwood-evals-svc).
- Covers onboarding (format & metadata), baseline benchmarking, periodic regression scans, triage and rollback criteria, and quantization validation.
- Excludes synthetic-only benchmarks (see related synthetic-benchmarks doc).

Ownership & Communication

- Primary owner: Applied ML (owner_team = engineering)
- Secondary owners: Model Onboarding squad, QA Platform
- Slack: #applied-ml-evals for live triage and escalation
- Pager for high-severity regressions: oncall-applied-ml (see eng-sre incident-playbook)

Onboarding checklist (prompt set creators)

1. Prepare prompt set following the format rules below.
2. Create an entry in the prompt catalog: prompt-catalog (include metadata fields).
3. Run the local eval-harness smoke test (cli steps below).
4. Submit a PR to the eval-harness prompt registry with a CI job that runs 1x baseline evaluation on the target model family.
5. Attach example usage and expected gold labels where relevant.
6. Notify reviewers and schedule a baseline review with Applied ML.

Prompt set formatting and metadata (required fields)

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | string | unique short id for the prompt set | customer-support-reply-050 |
| name | string | human readable name | Customer Support Reply |
| description | string | one-line summary of intent and scope | Responses to common billing FAQs |
| task_type | string | classification | classification / generation / semantic-search |
| dataset_source | string | origin (internal, customer, public) | internal |
| gold_labels | string[] | list of expected outputs for metric calculation | ["refund-yes","refund-no"] |
| expected_latency_ms | string | median target latency for golden examples | 150ms |
| evaluation_tags | string[] | tags used in dashboards | [regression-critical, hallucination-check] |

Formatting rules:
- Prompts must be UTF-8 and avoid personally identifiable information (PII). If customer data is required, use anonymized tokens and attach a data-approval ticket.
- Provide 100–1,000 examples for a production prompt set (min 30 for PoC).
- Each example should include: input, gold_label(s), optional context, and an example-level difficulty tag.

CLI smoke test (example)

1. Install eval-harness locally: pip install -e ./eval-harness
2. Run smoke eval: eval-harness run --prompt-set ./prompts/customer-support-reply-050.json --model rwinf-reasoner-v1 --output ./out.json
3. Verify gold label match and that the job completes under 2x expected_latency_ms.

Baseline benchmarking procedure

- Baseline frequency: on onboarding and on model version changes (e.g., rwinf-reasoner-v1 -> v1.1).
- Metrics collected: accuracy/F1 (classification), BLEU/ROUGE (generation), semantic-similarity (embeddings), hallucination-rate, latency (p50/p90/p99), token-cost.
- Baseline run config (recommended): 1,000 examples, beam_size=1, temperature=0.0 (deterministic baseline), num_repeats=3 for variability estimate.

Quality guardrails and alerting thresholds

- Regression detection: A regression is flagged when any of the following relative deltas occur vs baseline:
  - Accuracy / F1 drop >= 3% absolute (e.g., from 87% to 84%)
  - Hallucination-rate increases by >= 10% relative (e.g., from 5% to 5.5%)
  - Latency p90 increases by >= 25% absolute latency or exceeds SLA target
  - Token-cost per example increases by >= 15% for the same prompt set

- Severity levels:
  - Sev-1 (blocking): accuracy drop >= 7% OR hallucination-rate > 15% absolute OR user-facing SLA breach
  - Sev-2 (high): accuracy drop between 3–7% OR hallucination-rate increase between 10–15% relative
  - Sev-3 (low): marginal metric drift below alerting thresholds but trending

Automated monitoring & dashboards

- Eval-harness uploads baseline and periodic run results to data-warehouse table: evals.prompt_runs_v1.
- Dashboards: Grafana / Redash dashboards per prompt-set id with history and trendlines.
- Alerts: PagerDuty alerts for Sev-1/Sec-2 based on Prometheus rules that ingest eval metrics.

Regression triage workflow (step-by-step)

1. Detection: Alert triggers and an automated triage issue is created in JIRA (component: applied-ml-evals).
2. Triage owner assigned: oncall-applied-ml picks up within 1 hour.
3. Preliminary checks (15–30 min):
   a. Re-run eval-harness on the same commit/tag to confirm (idempotency check).
   b. Check model version, recent rollout history, and traffic routing (smart routing fallback activities).
   c. Verify data drift: sample input distribution checks vs baseline.
4. Classification: Determine root-cause bucket:
   - Model regression (new weights/rollout)
   - Quantization-induced regression
   - Serving/runtime change (kernel selection, batching policy)
   - Data/labeling change or prompt corruption
5. Remediation path by bucket:
   - Model regression: revert or canary rollback and open model-quality PR; run full evaluation suite across critical prompt sets.
   - Quantization: run quantization-rollback profile and compare outputs (see Quantization validation below).
   - Serving/runtime: compare runtime perf traces, p50/p90 latency, and KV cache hit rates; if kernel change identified, roll back.
   - Data issue: fix prompt-set then re-run baseline and close JIRA with tags.
6. Communication: Post update to JIRA and Slack channel including metrics snapshot, owner, and next steps.
7. Postmortem: For Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, initiate a postmortem within 48 hours and link to the incident review doc (oncall-and-incident-response).

Quantization validation checklist

- When a quantized model variant is added to the model catalog, run the following:
  - Perf check: token throughput and latency p50/p90 under representative batch distributions.
  - Functional check: run the full prompt set baseline and compare per-example outputs using similarity thresholds (BLEU / embedding cosine).
  - Delta mapping: record per-metric deltas and flag items exceeding the guardrail thresholds above.

- Quick test command: eval-harness run --prompt-set ./prompts/XXX.json --model rwinf-reasoner-v1-quantized --compare-to rwinf-reasoner-v1 --metrics similarity,accuracy --output quant-compare.json

Decision & Rollout policy recommendations

- Canary: For any new model variant (including quantized builds), rollout to 5% traffic and run continuous evals for 48 hrs against a set of critical prompt sets.
- Automatic fallback: If any Sev-1 condition is detected in canary, auto-fallback to the prior model variant and notify owners.
- Gold standard gating: Releases that touch models used by enterprise customers require manual sign-off from Applied ML and Product Security.

Examples & templates

- Prompt JSON template (snippet):
{
  "id": "customer-support-reply-050",
  "examples": [
    {"input": "My bill is too high this month", "gold_label": "offer-refund", "difficulty": "medium"}
  ]
}

- Evaluation CI job example (GitHub Actions):
name: prompt-set-eval
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  run-eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Run baseline eval
        run: eval-harness run --prompt-set ./prompts/$PROMPT_JSON --model $MODEL_TAG --output ./out.json

Post-incident review checklist

- Document timeline, root cause, remediation actions, and follow-up tasks.
- Update prompt set metadata if label or difficulty was incorrect.
- Create tickets for system improvements (observability, automated test coverage) and assign owners.

Appendix: Useful queries and utilities

- Quick query to get latest prompt-run metrics: SELECT * FROM evals.prompt_runs_v1 WHERE prompt_set_id = 'customer-support-reply-050' ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 50; (run in data-warehouse).
- Important configs:
  - Baseline-run size: baseline_examples=1000
  - Deterministic baseline: temperature=0.0
  - Canary window: 48h at 5% traffic
